title: Semantic Variability of Replies Across LLMs: Implications for Designing Conversation-Based Assessment
abstract: arXiv:2608.24920v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: This study examines whether LLM-generated replies remain semantically consistent when the underlying LLM changes. Using messages from real collaborative conversations, we compared the semantic similarity of generated replies across LLMs under two conditions: with and without preceding chat history. Results show that model choice and conversational context both affect response similarity and alignment with human replies. These findings indicate that prompting and conversational context alone may not be sufficient to preserve response consistency across LLMs, highlighting the need for infrastructure and design strategies that can maintain stable and comparable responses amid the rapid and continuous evolution of LLMs.

translated_title: 大语言模型回复的语义变异性：对设计基于对话评估的启示
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.24920v1 公告类型：新 摘要：本研究探讨了当底层大语言模型（LLM）发生变化时，其生成的回复是否在语义上保持一致。利用真实协作对话中的消息，我们在两种条件下（有和无先前聊天历史）比较了不同LLM生成回复的语义相似性。结果表明，模型选择和对话上下文都会影响回复的相似性及其与人类回复的一致性。这些发现表明，仅靠提示和对话上下文可能不足以跨LLM保持回复一致性，突显了在LLM快速持续演进中，需要基础设施和设计策略来维持稳定且可比较的回复。
tldr: 本研究揭示LLM模型选择和对话上下文均影响回复语义一致性，提示仅靠提示和上下文不足以确保跨模型稳定，需设计策略应对LLM演进。
en_tdlr: This study reveals that both model choice and conversational context affect semantic consistency of LLM replies, suggesting prompting and context alone are insufficient, necessitating design strategies amid LLM evolution.
